newsitem.title: USA: Brown & Williamson to challenge Fla. class-action.
newsitem.headline: Brown & Williamson to challenge Fla. class-action.

text.p: Tobacco group Brown & Williamson said on Friday it would seek to delay the scheduled September 8 trial start of a Florida class-action suit until Congress acts on a tentative global tobacco settlement announced a week ago.
But the trial judge, Alan Postman of Dade County Court, said the case on behalf of sick Florida smokers would proceed with pre-trial preparations throughout the summer.
"I am taking the position that unless there is an act of Congress, I have nothing to deal with," Postman said.

Only a conflict with another anti-tobacco lawsuit in another Miami court brought by the same lawyers, husband-and-wife Stanley and Susan Rosenblatt, was likely to cause a delay, Postman said during a hearing. Testimony in the current trial, on a $5 billion secondhand-smoke claim, is likely to begin on July 14 and may run two months or longer.

Michael Russ, an attorney for Brown & Williamson said the unit of B.A.T Industries Plc of Britain believed last week's settlement would cover class-action suits such as the Rosenblatts' and would shelter tobacco companies from punitive damages of the sort begin sought in the trial.
A lawyer for Philip Morris, another defendant in the case, said his company was preparing for trial without expectation of any immediate delay or resolution from last week's tentative agreement.
